text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a practice where developers frequently merge their code changes into a shared repository. Each time someone adds new code, automated builds start automatically. This means the software is compiled and checked without manual work. The system also runs tests to make sure everything works correctly. By doing this often, teams can catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines organize these steps, from building to testing to reporting results. This helps developers find bugs quickly and fix them fast. As a result, software quality improves, and releasing new versions becomes easier and safer for everyone.
